about.title: Cotati Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Cotati is a small city, and many residents get care at nearby Sonoma County clinics, urgent care centers, or hospitals in Rohnert Park and Santa Rosa. When something goes wrong during treatment, whether it's a missed diagnosis, a surgical mistake, or a medication error, patients are often left with more questions than answers. California law, through MICRA, sets specific and tight deadlines for these claims and requires a qualified medical expert to weigh in before a case can move forward. A bad medical result by itself doesn't mean malpractice occurred; the law requires showing that a provider fell below the accepted standard of care. Because these cases involve medical records, expert review, and strict notice requirements, contacting us early can help you understand whether you have a viable claim and what steps come next. Our team handles these cases, and there's no fee unless we recover on your behalf.

whyChoose.title: Why Timing and Evidence Matter in Cotati Malpractice Cases

items.title: Strict Filing Deadlines
items.desc: California generally requires malpractice claims to be filed within one year of discovering the injury, and no more than three years from when it happened. A 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider is also required before filing, so early action matters.

items.title: Expert Review Is Required
items.desc: California law almost always requires a qualified medical expert to review the case and confirm the standard of care was not met. This step is essential before a malpractice claim can proceed.

items.title: Damages Caps Apply But Change Yearly
items.desc: California places a statutory cap on non-economic damages in malpractice cases, though that cap rises each year under current law. We can explain how this may apply to your specific circumstances.

items.question: How do I know if a bad medical outcome was actually malpractice?
items.answer: Not every poor result from treatment counts as malpractice under California law. It has to be shown that a provider's care fell below an accepted medical standard, which is why a qualified expert review is almost always required. We can help evaluate your medical records to see if that standard applies to your case.

items.question: I live in Cotati but was treated at a hospital outside the city. Does that matter?
items.answer: No, it doesn't limit your options. Many Cotati residents receive care in Rohnert Park, Santa Rosa, or elsewhere in Sonoma County, and California's malpractice laws apply regardless of which facility provided treatment. What matters is where the care happened and when you discovered the harm.

items.question: How does your firm handle medical malpractice cases?
items.answer: We handle medical malpractice cases and typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover money for you. We'll review your medical records and help you understand whether you have a viable claim under California law.
